The most powerful refutation is that the felicific calculus falsely assumes pleasures and pains are commensurable on a single quantitative scale, when in reality they differ irreducibly in kind, quality, and meaning. This objection shows that Bentham’s method cannot capture what actually makes lives go well or badly, making it conceptually incoherent as a measure of well-being. Therefore, neither of the two provided options is the most powerful refutation.

CONFIDENCE: 92
